attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as router between lan-a (vtnet1/opt1, 10.60.10.0/24, peering node2's eth1) and lan-b (vtnet2/opt2, 10.60.20.0/24, peering node3's eth1). Added default-deny-overriding pass rules for both interfaces plus a directional hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule (OPNsense/Firewall/Filter/snatrules) that translates lan-a→lan-b traffic to node1's lan-b address (10.60.20.1), while leaving lan-b→lan-a traffic untouched. Verified with live TCP connections: node2→node3 traffic arrives at node3 sourced from 10.60.20.1 (node1), while node3→node2 traffic arrives at node2 sourced from node3's own address (10.60.20.2), confirming the required asymmetric NAT behavior. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node2, node3, then node1/router), proving changed boot identity on each (Linux boot_id for node2/node3, FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1) and re-verifying full recovery of interface config, firewall/NAT rules, and the exact directional-NAT connection behavior after each restart.
